page: Amazon Web Services x8i.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture running at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 2048.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, but offers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the x8i.32xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core, Passmark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read-only small block bandwidth and strong large-block read/write performance. The processor's support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) drives top-tier results in extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Additionally, it delivers top-tier performance in Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside top-tier prompt processing speeds for large language models.

This instance represents a highly resource-dense configuration tailored for memory-intensive workloads. While single-core CPU performance and Passmark memory scores sit in the average tier, the massive 2 TB memory capacity and high multi-core density offer qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require large datasets to reside entirely in memory. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage. The hardware profile is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based LLM inference tasks.
